chunks: And from him, from Abdul Momine, from Ali ibn Abu Hama, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
A dirham you spend in the Hajj is superior to twenty thousand dirhams you spend in a right (charity/obligation).

key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A dirham, a unit of currency

ai.seo_question: Why is spending a small amount on Hajj considered better than spending a large amount on charity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual weight of Hajj by comparing a modest expenditure there against a substantial sum in general charity (haqq), underscoring the pilgrimage's unique status as a primary act of worship. This comparison reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the qualitative superiority of Hajj over quantitative charity, linking it to the concept of 'ibadah' that encompasses both physical and financial sacrifice. The narration serves as a practical reminder for believers to prioritize the fulfillment of the Hajj obligation even with limited means, rather than deferring it for greater wealth.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Abdul Momine, from Ali Bin Abu Hama, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A Dirham you spend in the Hajj is superior than the twenty thousand Dirhams you spend regarding a right’.
en.sarwar: 15. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from ‘Abd al-Mu’min from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
one dirham that you spend for Hajj is better than twenty thousand dirham which you spent for a truth (a right).”
